entries.text: Save your Thalers when you can. Walking between districts is free.
The bus stops running at night. If you stay out late, be ready to walk.
Find a bench when your Energy runs low. Resting advances one part of the day.
A bed or sofa lets you sleep until the next morning. Plan your deliveries before turning in.
You only have six inventory slots before bags. Leave room for whatever you hope to bring home.
Read the taskboards if you need work. A delivery can put Thalers in your pocket without a fight.
People move through the day. Ask about their routines before you go looking for them.
Keep some Thalers on you. Banknotes in a suitcase cannot pay your bus fare or shopping bill.
Use a container to store things you cannot carry. Ordinary storage costs nothing.
The streets are more dangerous at night. Finish ordinary errands before the light goes.
Check your existing stacks before abandoning useful supplies. A partly filled stack may still have room.
Talk to people before walking away. Some jobs are offered in conversation rather than on a board.
A canvas backpack, duffel bag or briefcase adds carrying space, though the bag itself takes a slot.
Two bags of the same kind do not give twice the space. Different bag types are more useful together.
Read an item's requirements before buying it. Owning a tool does not mean you know how to use it.
Training books improve your skills while you carry them. Put a book away and its bonus ends.
A trader pays less than they charge. Check the offered price before selling something you might need again.
Sleeping saves your progress once you wake. Resting on a bench does not.
Traders and renewable indoor supplies refresh in the morning. Coming back the same afternoon will not refill them.
Outdoor supplies appear at night. Unclaimed stock is cleared in the morning, so decide whether a trip is worth the risk.
Keep track of your keys. A matching key can save you a lockpick and a dangerous delay at a door.
A failed or abandoned lockpicking attempt costs a lockpick. Make sure you have time to finish.
A successful lockpicking attempt keeps your lockpick. Press Enter again after unlocking to open the way.
Resting saves Energy, but time still passes and costs Sanity. A bench is not a way to stop the clock.
A gun needs compatible ammunition in your carried inventory. Ammunition stored elsewhere will not help in a fight.
Knowing how to handle a gun is only half the job. Its ammunition can have requirements of its own.
Medicine skill improves recovery. Look at the recovery preview before spending supplies you may need later.
Hide before an officer spots you. Once detected, you cannot slip into hiding inside a living patrol's reach.
Opening your inventory does not stop a fight. Get somewhere safe before sorting your belongings.
Leave inventory space for a job's supplies and reward. A full bag can stop you accepting work or collecting payment.
Read a shipment's deadline before taking it. Night pickups and morning handovers leave little room for extra errands.
Bench rest does not replace sleep. Stay awake too long and the extra Sanity costs will catch up with you.
Your own deposits survive supply refreshes. A morning restock does not erase the things you put away.
Watch the shrinking attack ring. Releasing near its center hits harder than releasing at its widest point.
Militia can draw a gun after you hurt them. Starting a fight can be far worse than being spotted.
Raising a vital limit does not heal you. New equipment may give you room to recover, but you still need recovery.
Dusan trades before you finish his jobs. Look through his stock if you need a way to improve your lockpicking.
Apartment 21 has an unlocked floor suitcase for your belongings. Stash spare goods there before a long trip.
A Courier night pass helps with routine militia detection. It will not protect you from monsters or a fight you started.
Find-and-deliver requests pay twice the item's listed price. That can be a better return than selling it to a trader.
A monster's fear can reach farther than its detection. If your Sanity is slipping, put more distance between you.
Shipment crates belong to active jobs. Accept the right contract before making a dangerous trip to collect one.
Patrol blows land when the attack animation finishes. Moving out of reach before then can save you.
Some delivery goods can be sold like ordinary items. Check your active jobs before selling supplies meant for someone else.
Permanent gear grants its bonuses just by being in your inventory. Different item types combine, but duplicate copies give no extra bonus.
Sleeping straight through to morning does not create a skipped night's outdoor loot. Night scavenging requires being there.
Several shipment jobs use the same district crate. Read the active objective rather than searching for a new crate for every contract.
A full bag cannot always be stored or sold: removing it also removes its extra slots. Unload other goods first.
Ask your questions before demanding Thalers. Someone you intimidate will refuse conversation for the rest of the day.
Habits shape you permanently. In each competing perk pair, the first trait you earn closes off its rival.
